title: Partition String
statement:
Cut `s` into segments from left to right with this rule. Begin with an empty piece and append the characters of `s` to it one at a time. The moment the piece is a string that has not already been cut as a segment, it becomes the next segment and a fresh empty piece begins at the following character. If `s` ends while the piece is still a string cut earlier, those leftover characters are discarded.

Return the segments as a list of strings, in the order they were cut.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

The procedure is fully specified, so simulate it: grow a piece one character at a time and cut it off the moment it is a string that was never cut before. The only real question is how to ask "cut before?" quickly. Scanning the list of earlier segments works for short strings but costs time proportional to the whole list; a set of the segments answers each lookup in time proportional to the piece's length.

## Approach

1. Keep `seen` (a set of the segments cut so far), `segments` (the answer, in order) and `current` (the piece being grown, initially empty).
2. For each character `char` of `s`, append it to `current`.
3. If `seen.has(current)` is false, add `current` to `seen`, push it onto `segments`, and reset `current` to the empty string.
4. When `s` ends, return `segments`. A non-empty `current` left over was cut before, so it is dropped.

## Example 1, step by step

For `s = "abbccccd"`: `"a"` is new, so cut it; `"b"` is new, cut. The next `"b"` is in `seen`, so `current` grows to `"bc"`, which is new: cut. `"c"` is new: cut. The next `"c"` is seen, so it grows to `"cc"`: cut. Finally `"d"` is new: cut. The result is `["a", "b", "bc", "c", "cc", "d"]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n√n): a piece reaches length L only after its L - 1 shorter prefixes were all cut earlier, so their lengths 1 + 2 + ... + (L - 1) fit within n and L is at most about √(2n); each step builds and hashes a piece of that length.
- Space: O(n): the strings in `seen` and `segments` have total length at most n.

## Pitfalls

- Leftover characters at the end are dropped, not added: `"aaaa"` gives `["a", "aa"]`, not `["a", "aa", "a"]`.
- Reset `current` only after a cut; when the piece is already in `seen`, keep growing it instead of starting over.
- Looking pieces up in the `segments` list instead of a set makes every step scan all earlier segments, which is far too slow for `s.length` near 10^5.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seen` | set of the segments cut so far |
| `segments` | the answer, in the order the segments were cut |
| `current` | the piece grown since the last cut |
| `char` | the next character of `s` |

narration.2: seen holds every segment cut so far, so lookups are fast.
narration.3: segments collects the answer in the order the pieces are cut.
narration.4: current is the piece grown since the last cut.
narration.5: Read s one character at a time.
narration.6: Extend the current piece by this character.
narration.7: Has this exact piece never been cut before?
narration.8: It is new: remember it in seen...
narration.10: ...and start an empty piece at the next character.
narration.13: Any leftover piece was already cut before, so it is dropped; return the segments.
